# Phase-d: requirements that must change before the plan can run

From: randlee (owner). To: run-lead@run.
Reviewed: plan/phase-d at 5cffe24, gated text under gate-items-f5244e0.

Phase-d keeps its shape and its sprints. This is not a redesign. Each item
is a requirement change, one small example of why, and the current text it
will not pass against. Make the changes, check drift, report.

## 1. Monty gets its own crate: sc-monty

Change: create sc-monty.
- Wave 1. Depends on the pydantic Monty crates only. No sc-* crates, no
  tokio, no serde_json, no cron types or cron-reserved names.
- All logic for calling Monty lives there: compile, session, limits,
  host-function dispatch, typed errors, session to bytes and back.
- Surface: a compiled session plus MontyInvoke<Tin, Tout> (script, function
  name, inputs -> output). Phase-d delivers the value-level form only.
- sc-cron depends on sc-monty. JSON conversion and serde_json stay in
  sc-cron. Hook behavior and tests are ported, not deleted or weakened;
  hooks keep receiving values, not JSON strings.
- The d-10 command transform calls sc-monty directly.

Example: an app generated with postgres and no cron wants one Monty
transform. Today Monty exists only inside sc-cron and the template enables
it with `monty = ["cron", ...]`, so that app cannot have it. d-10 answers
by writing a second host in the service.

Will not pass against:
- d-10: "do not copy the scheduler feed/session/host machinery or add a
  sc-cron dependency to no-cron layouts. sc-cron retains its
  scheduler-specific host."
- REQ-RUN-0002, REQ-RUN-0702, NFR-RUN-0009 as amended in d-5 for EIGHT
  public 0.3.0 crates. It is nine; sc-monty publishes in the first wave.
- REQ-CRON-0001 and the sc-cron manifest, which own the Monty dependency
  directly.
- PRD section 2, which lists Monty as its own part of sc-runtime.

## 2. sc-cron saves the compiled Monty binary

Change:
- When a hook's source compiles, sc-cron saves the compiled session as a
  blob in a table that is part of sc-cron, a row type through Storage<T>.
- Key: SHA-256 of the source, computed with the sc-sha crate, plus Monty's
  dump version.
- The source text in the schedule row stays the source of truth. A blob is
  used only when its key matches that source.
- Any load failure (unreadable version, corrupt bytes, missing cron_stop or
  cron_tick) is a cache miss: recompile from source and overwrite.
- The blob is captured immediately after compile, before any run. No run
  state is persisted.
- Compile when the schedule is written, so a script that does not compile
  is rejected at submit instead of at its first tick.

Example: the daemon restarts. A schedule whose source has not changed runs
its next tick without recompiling.

Will not pass against:
- ANC-012. sc-sha is published from the sc-compose repo. Owner ruling:
  sc-sha is permitted as a production dependency; ANC-012 covers the
  sc-compose composition crates and ATM crates. Propose the amended anchor
  wording and its deterministic check.
- ANC-034. The table is sc-cron's own row type; no backend gains code for it.
- d-9, which has no blob table, migration or compile-at-write step.
- Today's behavior: compile happens only on the first run of a generation.

## 3. A Monty transform's source is data, changeable at run time

Change: the source of a Monty command transform is loaded at run time and
can be replaced without rebuilding the app.

Example: cron already works this way; the hook source is in the schedule
row. A transform compiled into the binary gives no reason to use Monty.

Will not pass against: d-10, which does not say where transform source
comes from.

## 4. The command seam is provisional in 0.3.0

Change: Transform, storage_read and storage_write are documented as not yet
stable. Their shape must not prevent adding later, without breaking
consumers: (a) a second input to the transform, (b) an outcome that writes
nothing, (c) a transform that runs inside an atomic transaction. An outcome
that writes nothing is still a typed Result: Ok with nothing written is
distinct from Err. Build none of these now. Forbid none of them.

Example: "create this widget only if no widget has that name" has to read
before it decides and sometimes writes nothing.
storage_write(store, transform, input) takes one input and always writes.

Will not pass against:
- ADR-RUN-0021, "Open, owner decides, nothing assumed", item 2: how an app
  supplies its transform and what the transform may call. d-10 decides it
  and d-12 publishes it to crates.io.
- d-10: "Transaction bodies may not call this mechanism or await
  interpreter/I/O." Reword as phase-d scope ("not built in phase-d"), not
  as a prohibition (PRD-ENG-5).

## 5. Cron commands use the shared command path

Change: an end user schedules cron with a Monty or Python script plus JSON
data that is passed to the script. A consuming app can modify or append to
that JSON before it is written. That step is the transform. Name which cron
commands go through the shared path; for any that do not, state the reason
in the sprint text.

Example: atm-core appends its own data to the user's JSON when a schedule
is added, so the end user does not supply it. Command type in, transform
appends, CronRow written through Storage<CronRow>.

Will not pass against: PRD-CRON-5 and ADR-RUN-0021 point 6 ("Cron follows
this pattern"). d-9 never references the shared path, and d-10 is validated
with no cron selected.

## 6. Default plain conversion, and nothing "must be hand-written"

Change:
- A command whose Tcli converts directly to Tsql needs no hand-written
  transform.
- No ADR or REQ may state that the command path must be hand-written.
  Generators come in a follow-up phase and run in a consuming project
  against a delivered sc-runtime. Hand-written code is the interim form.

Example: a command type and a row type with the same fields.

Will not pass against:
- ADR-RUN-0021 point 3 ("The default is a plain conversion; an app replaces
  it where it has rules"). d-10 makes every transform application-written.
- REQ-RUN-0318 ("crates/sc-runtime contains no generator") if it is read as
  forbidding a consumer-side generator. Scan the REQ/ADR set for any other
  wording that binds hand-writing or forbids generators.

## 7. The template example uses the path

Change: state which of the widget create/get/delete commands go through
storage_read/storage_write. At least one write and one read must.

Will not pass against: PRD-CMD-1. d-10 routes create and delete through a
WidgetStorage extension and does not say what uses the shared path. If all
three already do, say so in one line.

## 8. Transactions keep the option of their own retry policy

Change: engine defaults for retry are fine. Remove the rule that retry can
only ever be engine configuration.

Will not pass against: d-5, "Only name/mode are transaction properties;
finite retry/deadline policy belongs to engine configuration, not the
transaction spec" (PRD-ENG-5).

## 9. Ratification

ADR-RUN-0020 and ADR-RUN-0021 are still Proposed, and d-5 says d-6..d-12
must not start against Proposed ADRs. Send me the exact contract to ratify
as one short list.

before.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with only transaction name/mode properties. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Eight published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-storage first, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.
